course.title: Applied Statistics and Queuing Theory
course.department: Department of Computer Science and Engineering

content.value: An engineering professor purchases a new computer every two years with preference for three (14) models: M1, M2 and M3. If the present model is M1, the next computer may be M2 with probability 0·2 or M3 with probability 0·15. If the present model is M2, the probabilities of switching to M1 and M3 are 0·6 and 0·25, respectively. And, if the present model is M3, then the probabilities of switching to M1 and M2 are 0·5 and 0·1, respectively.
i) Determine the probability that the professor will purchase the current model in four years.
ii) Determine the steady-state probability distribution of this problem.

_source_title: B.Sc. Engineering 3rd Year 2nd Term Regular Examination, 2021
